        with:
          tool: just@1.58.0
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          components: llvm-tools-preview
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@f7e5d7c961414b23f5b25b2da9294395d08513ad # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-llvm-cov
      - run: just coverage 90
      # Non-blocking for now: the workspace-total gate above can pass while
      # a small crate is far below threshold (a few large crates dominate
      # the total line count). Visible in logs so regressions get noticed;
      # promote to a required check once existing per-crate gaps are closed.
      - run: just coverage-per-crate 90 || echo "::warning::one or more crates below 90% line coverage (non-blocking, see job log above)"

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@f7e5d7c961414b23f5b25b2da9294395d08513ad # v2

          tool: just@1.58.0
      - uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095 # v0
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@f7e5d7c961414b23f5b25b2da9294395d08513ad # v2

          tool: cargo-deny

  validate:
    name: Validate Changesets & Workspace Status
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

  release-asset-attestation:
    name: Release Asset Attestation
    # Fork PRs also receive a read-only GITHUB_TOKEN and only lack secrets; same-repo-only is a cost/policy choice.
    if: github.event_name == 'push' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      ASSET: callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz

        id: latest

          fi
          echo "tag=$tag" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

        if: steps.latest.outputs.tag != ''

          set -euo pipefail
          gh release download "$TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$ASSET" --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP"

        if: steps.latest.outputs.tag != ''
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          verify() {
            gh attestation verify "$1" \
              --repo orin-dx/callisto \
              --signer-workflow orin-dx/callisto/.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml \
              --deny-self-hosted-runners
          }
          verify "$RUNNER_TEMP/$ASSET"
          # Negative control: a modified copy must fail, so the pass above is not vacuous.
          cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/$ASSET" "$RUNNER_TEMP/tampered.tar.gz"
          printf 'x' >> "$RUNNER_TEMP/tampered.tar.gz"
          if verify "$RUNNER_TEMP/tampered.tar.gz"; then
            echo "::error::negative control failed: attestation verification accepted a tampered copy of $ASSET"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "negative control passed: the tampered copy was rejected"

content.content:
name: Release

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      release_source_sha:
        description: 'Merged managed release-PR commit to recover; leave empty for the triggering commit.'
        required: false
        type: string

permissions: {}

# One group per commit: GitHub replaces a pending run in a shared group, which
# could silently drop a release merge queued behind an unrelated push.
concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  verify:
    name: Verify release candidate
    if: github.event_name == 'push' || inputs.release_source_sha == ''
    timeout-minutes: 45
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Build local Callisto
        uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local

      - name: Install just
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@f7e5d7c961414b23f5b25b2da9294395d08513ad # v2
        with:
          tool: just@1.58.0

      - name: Format Check
        run: just fmt-check

      - name: Clippy Lints
        run: just lint

      - name: Install release verification tools
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@f7e5d7c961414b23f5b25b2da9294395d08513ad # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-nextest,ripgrep

      - name: Unit & Integration Tests
        run: just test

      - name: Install cargo-deny
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@f7e5d7c961414b23f5b25b2da9294395d08513ad # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-deny

      - name: Supply Chain Audit
        run: just audit

      - name: Verify workflow contracts and reject mutable action references
        run: just workflow-contracts

  recovery-checks:
    name: Check release workflow policy for recovery
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.release_source_sha != ''
    timeout-minutes: 10
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Install ripgrep
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@f7e5d7c961414b23f5b25b2da9294395d08513ad # v2
        with:
          tool: ripgrep
      - name: Install just
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@f7e5d7c961414b23f5b25b2da9294395d08513ad # v2
        with:
          tool: just@1.58.0
      - name: Verify release workflow contracts
        run: just release-workflow-checks

  release-candidate:
    name: Identify a merged Callisto release PR
    needs: [verify, recovery-checks]
    # Exactly one gate runs per event; a failed gate matches neither clause.
    if: >-
      always() && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' &&
      ((needs.verify.result == 'success' && needs.recovery-checks.result == 'skipped') ||
       (needs.recovery-checks.result == 'success' && needs.verify.result == 'skipped'))
    timeout-minutes: 10
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      is_release_pr: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.is_release_pr }}
      release_source_sha: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
      orchestration_sha: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
    steps:
      - id: candidate
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA_INPUT: ${{ inputs.release_source_sha }}
          TRIGGERING_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          release_source_sha="${RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA_INPUT:-$TRIGGERING_SHA}"
          if [[ ! "$release_source_sha" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::release_source_sha must be exactly 40 lowercase hex characters"
            exit 1
          fi
          resolved_sha=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${release_source_sha}" --jq '.sha')
          if [[ "$resolved_sha" != "$release_source_sha" ]]; then
            echo "::error::release_source_sha does not resolve to that exact commit"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Attestations are stamped with this run's own SHA, so the
          # coordinator must be exactly the revision running this workflow.
          orchestration_sha="$TRIGGERING_SHA"
          # This only schedules the job. `release plan` verifies the actual
          # parent-to-merge delta; labels and PR metadata are never authority.
          # The GitHub API check is complementary provenance evidence: a
          # trusted merge must be both an actual merge of the managed PR and
          # a GitHub-verified signed commit. It cannot be a direct push.
          prs=$(gh api --paginate "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${release_source_sha}/pulls" --jq '[.[] | select(.merged_at != null and .base.ref == "main" and .head.repo.full_name == "'"${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"'" and (.head.ref == "callisto/version-packages" or (.head.ref | test("^callisto/version-packages--[0-9a-f]{40}$"))))] | length')
          verified=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${release_source_sha}" --jq '.commit.verification.verified')
          if [[ "$prs" == 1 && "$verified" == true ]]; then
            {
              echo 'is_release_pr=true'
              echo "release_source_sha=$release_source_sha"
              echo "orchestration_sha=$orchestration_sha"
            } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo 'is_release_pr=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  version-pr:
    name: Create or update the Callisto release PR
    needs: release-candidate
    if: >-
      always() && needs.release-candidate.result == 'success' &&
      needs.release-candidate.outputs.is_release_pr != 'true' &&
      inputs.release_source_sha == ''
    timeout-minutes: 10
    concurrency:
      group: version-pr
      cancel-in-progress: false
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    outputs:
      has_pending_changesets: ${{ steps.version-pr.outputs.hasChangesets }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - name: Compose, version, and open the release PR
        id: version-pr
        uses: $/.github/actions/callisto-action
        with:
          setup_callisto: 'false'
          branch: main
          release_branch: callisto/version-packages
          # Interdependent Cargo packages bump together, so Cargo.lock must be refreshed in the release PR.
          version_command: 'callisto version --refresh-lockfiles'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

  plan:
    name: Derive ephemeral intent from the merged release commit
    needs: release-candidate
    # always(): release-candidate's own ancestors include a gate that is skipped
    # by design, and a skipped ancestor silently skips any job without a status function.
    if: >-
      always() && needs.release-candidate.result == 'success' &&
      needs.release-candidate.outputs.is_release_pr == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 20
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      has_artifacts: ${{ steps.slots.outputs.has_artifacts }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # The coordinator must be the current workflow revision. Recovery
          # never rebuilds its release engine from historic source.
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
          path: release-source
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Derive and hash intent
        env:
          RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
          ORCHESTRATION_SHA: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          handoff_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent"
          mkdir -p "$handoff_dir"
          callisto release plan --source-root "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/release-source" \
            --orchestration-revision "$ORCHESTRATION_SHA" --artifact-repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
            --from-release-commit "$RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA" \
            --decision "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/release-source/.callisto/release-decision.json" \
            --out "$handoff_dir/release-intent.json"
          # Relative name: the consumers verify from a different runner OS and RUNNER_TEMP.
          (cd "$handoff_dir" && shasum -a 256 release-intent.json > release-intent.json.sha256)
      - name: Read declared artifact slot count
        id: slots
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Own statement: set -e cannot see a substitution failing inside an echo argument.
          has_artifacts=$(jq '.artifactSlots | length > 0' "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent/release-intent.json")
          case "$has_artifacts" in
            true|false) ;;
            *) echo "::error::artifact slot probe returned '$has_artifacts'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          echo "has_artifacts=$has_artifacts" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
          if-no-files-found: error
          # 1 day was too short: a stuck run needing "execute" re-run days
          # later (e.g. while a workflow bug gets diagnosed and fixed) loses
          # this artifact before the fix even lands, forcing a full rerun
          # instead of just the failed job.
          retention-days: 7

  build-artifact:
    name: Build ${{ matrix.target }} from the intent-bound source tree
    needs: [plan, release-candidate]
    if: always() && needs.plan.result == 'success' && needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 45
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - id: macos-arm64
            runner: macos-14
            target: aarch64-apple-darwin
            asset: callisto-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz
            kind: cli
          - id: linux-gnu
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
            asset: callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz
            kind: cli
          - id: linux-musl
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            target: x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
            asset: callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz
            kind: cross
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    permissions:
      contents: read
      attestations: write
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
          path: release-source
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
      - name: Verify handoff
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          handoff_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent"
          (cd "$handoff_dir" && shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256)
          callisto release inspect --input "$handoff_dir/release-intent.json"
          mkdir -p "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-artifacts"
      - name: Build declared artifact
        env:
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_KIND: ${{ matrix.kind }}
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_TARGET: ${{ matrix.target }}
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_ASSET: ${{ matrix.asset }}
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_SOURCE_ROOT: ${{ github.workspace }}/release-source
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts
        run: |
          bash .github/scripts/build-release-artifact.sh
      - name: Attest exact artifact bytes
        uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@4d101475d8b20a2381f78447822ac1eab6504dd8 # v4.2.2
        with:
          subject-path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts/${{ matrix.asset }}
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: release-build-${{ matrix.id }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts/${{ matrix.asset }}
          if-no-files-found: error

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build one declared Callisto product artifact. This script deliberately owns
# only platform compilation and archive layout; Callisto owns all release
# planning, artifact identity, provenance verification, and publication.
set -euo pipefail

: "${CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_KIND:?must name cli or cross}"
: "${CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_TARGET:?must name a supported Rust target}"
: "${CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_ASSET:?must name the expected release asset}"
: "${CALLISTO_RELEASE_SOURCE_ROOT:?must name the checked-out source root}"
: "${CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_DIR:?must name an output directory}"

kind="$CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_KIND"
target="$CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_TARGET"
asset="$CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_ASSET"
source_root="$CALLISTO_RELEASE_SOURCE_ROOT"
artifact_dir="$CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_DIR"

case "$kind:$target:$asset" in
  cli:aarch64-apple-darwin:callisto-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz | \
  cli:x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu:callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz | \
  cross:x86_64-unknown-linux-musl:callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz)
    ;;
  *)
    printf 'unsupported Callisto release artifact: kind=%s target=%s asset=%s\n' \
      "$kind" "$target" "$asset" >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

mkdir -p "$artifact_dir"

case "$kind" in
  cli)
    rustup target add "$target"
    (cd "$source_root" && cargo build --locked --release -p callisto-cli --target "$target")
    tar -C "$source_root/target/$target/release" -czf "$artifact_dir/$asset" callisto
    ;;
  cross)
    rustup target add "$target"
    cargo install cross --locked --version 0.2.5
    (cd "$source_root" && cross build --locked --release -p callisto-cli --target "$target")
    tar -C "$source_root/target/$target/release" -czf "$artifact_dir/$asset" callisto
    ;;
esac
version: 2

updates:
  - package-ecosystem: github-actions
    directory: /
    schedule:
      interval: weekly
    cooldown:
      default-days: 7
    open-pull-requests-limit: 3
    groups:
      routine-actions:
        applies-to: version-updates
        patterns: ["*"]
      security-actions:
        applies-to: security-updates
        patterns: ["*"]

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build one declared Callisto product artifact. This script deliberately owns
# only platform compilation and archive layout; Callisto owns all release
# planning, artifact identity, provenance verification, and publication.
set -euo pipefail

: "${CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_KIND:?must name cli or cross}"
: "${CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_TARGET:?must name a supported Rust target}"
: "${CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_ASSET:?must name the expected release asset}"
: "${CALLISTO_RELEASE_SOURCE_ROOT:?must name the checked-out source root}"
: "${CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_DIR:?must name an output directory}"

kind="$CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_KIND"
target="$CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_TARGET"
asset="$CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_ASSET"
source_root="$CALLISTO_RELEASE_SOURCE_ROOT"
artifact_dir="$CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_DIR"

case "$kind:$target:$asset" in
  cli:aarch64-apple-darwin:callisto-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz | \
  cli:x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu:callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz | \
  cross:x86_64-unknown-linux-musl:callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz)
    ;;
  *)
    printf 'unsupported Callisto release artifact: kind=%s target=%s asset=%s\n' \
      "$kind" "$target" "$asset" >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

mkdir -p "$artifact_dir"

case "$kind" in
  cli)
    rustup target add "$target"
    (cd "$source_root" && cargo build --locked --release -p callisto-cli --target "$target")
    tar -C "$source_root/target/$target/release" -czf "$artifact_dir/$asset" callisto
    ;;
  cross)
    rustup target add "$target"
    cargo install cross --locked --version 0.2.5
    (cd "$source_root" && cross build --locked --release -p callisto-cli --target "$target")
    tar -C "$source_root/target/$target/release" -czf "$artifact_dir/$asset" callisto
    ;;
esac

Dependency-aware, changeset-driven versioning and releases for Cargo, npm, and PyPI monorepos.

--- Callisto turns per-package changesets into a version plan for Cargo, npm/pnpm, and Python/PyPI workspaces. It reads native manifests to decide which dependents need updates, then prepares the files and release operations for review. ## A change through Callisto Suppose `service` depends on a Cargo crate `core` at `^0.2`. A contributor records a minor change to `core`: ```sh callisto add --package cargo/core:minor --summary "Add streaming API" callisto version --dry-run ``` With the default cascade policy, the plan is: | Package | Before | Planned change | | --- | --- | --- | | `core` | `0.2.0` | `0.3.0` from the changeset | | `service` | `1.4.2`, requires `core ^0.2` | `1.4.3` from the default patch cascade; requirement updated to `^0.3` | | Unrelated npm or Python package | Its current version | No bump just because it shares the repo | The dependency requirement triggers the `service` bump; sharing a repo does not. Callisto does not infer arbitrary cross-language dependencies. Explicit version groups can couple packages that should move together. - `callisto version` updates affected manifests, lockfiles, and changelogs for review and commit. - The release workflow uses native publishers and coordinates configured tags, GitHub releases, and assets. Package owners retain their hooks and credentials. ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'flowchart': {'curve': 'basis', 'nodeSpacing': 40, 'rankSpacing': 56}, 'themeVariables': {'fontFamily': 'Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif', 'fontSize': '14px', 'lineColor': '#94a3b8', 'edgeLabelBackground': '#ffffff'}}}%% flowchart LR classDef source fill:#eef2ff,stroke:#6366f1,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#1e1b4b,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; classDef store fill:#f8fafc,stroke:#64748b,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#0f172a,rx:10px,ry:10px; classDef engine fill:#f5f3ff,stroke:#8b5cf6,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#4c1d95,rx:10px,ry:10px; classDef router fill:#fffbeb,stroke:#f59e0b,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#78350f,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; classDef output fill:#ecfdf5,stroke:#10b981,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#064e3b,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; changesets["Changesets
release intent"] --> plan["Version plan

(2 filtered) [see remaining: tail -n +1 "$HOME/Library/Application Support/rtk/tee/1792521676_ls-hidden.log"] # Security Policy ## Reporting a Vulnerability Email **security@orin-dx.com** — don't open a public issue for anything that could be exploited before a fix ships. Include: - Which crate or code path is affected - The concrete failure scenario — what an attacker could do, and how - Steps to reproduce, if you have them Expect an acknowledgment within 5 business days. We'll keep you posted as a fix moves through triage, and credit you in the release notes unless you'd rather stay anonymous. ## Scope Callisto edits manifests and pushes releases across multiple package registries from inside CI, so the threat model is higher-stakes than a typical CLI tool: - **Registry token exposure** — Callisto's own release workflow (`.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`) grants `contents`/`pull-requests` write only to the jobs that need them (`version-pr`, `execute`); registry credentials (`CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, and `NPM_TOKEN`/`TWINE_PASSWORD` for workspaces that publish npm/PyPI packages) reach only the `execute` job. A way to make Callisto, or the in-repo `.github/actions/callisto-action`, exfiltrate those tokens, or publish to a package other than the one it was asked to, is a critical finding. - **Workflow/action injection** — Callisto is designed to run unattended on `push` to `main` in downstream repos. An untrusted PR that could get its content executed by the release workflow (rather than merely analyzed) is in scope. - **Manifest parser safety** — `callisto-manifests` edits `Cargo.toml`/`package.json` via CST-preserving parsers (`toml_edit`, `serde_json`) rather than regex specifically to avoid corruption; a crafted manifest that causes incorrect writes, path traversal, or a crash mid-write (bypassing the atomic `NamedTempFile` + `fs::rename` guarantee) is a real finding. - **Version/changelog spoofing** — a way to make `callisto version` compute or apply an incorrect bump, or inject arbitrary content into a generated changelog, that a maintainer could plausibly merge without noticing. - **Git operation safety** — `callisto_model::vcs` runs the system `git` binary; argument injection through ref names or paths, or unsafe handling of an untrusted repository (submodules, refs, hooks), is in scope. Dependency vulnerabilities are already checked continuously via `just audit` (`cargo deny check advisories`) in CI — a report that only restates an existing advisory `cargo audit`/`cargo deny` already flags isn't a new finding, but a way to bypass or disable that check is. Out of scope: vulnerabilities in Cargo, npm, PyPI, or GitHub Actions themselves — report those to the respective platform. ## Supported Versions Security fixes land on `main` and the latest published release of each affected crate. Given Callisto is pre-1.0, older minor versions are not backported — upgrade to the latest release.

An untrusted PR that could get its content executed by the release workflow (rather than merely analyzed) is in scope. - **Manifest parser safety** — `callisto-manifests` edits `Cargo.toml`/`package.json` via CST-preserving parsers (`toml_edit`, `serde_json`) rather than regex specifically to avoid corruption; a crafted manifest that causes incorrect writes, path traversal, or a crash mid-write (bypassing the atomic `NamedTempFile` + `fs::rename` guarantee) is a real finding. - **Version/changelog spoofing** — a way to make `callisto version` compute or apply an incorrect bump, or inject arbitrary content into a generated changelog, that a maintainer could plausibly merge without noticing. - **Git operation safety** — `callisto_model::vcs` runs the system `git` binary; argument injection through ref names or paths, or unsafe handling of an untrusted repository (submodules, refs, hooks), is in scope. Dependency vulnerabilities are already checked continuously via `just audit` (`cargo deny check advisories`) in CI — a report that only restates an existing advisory `cargo audit`/`cargo deny` already flags isn't a new finding, but a way to bypass or disable that check is. Out of scope: vulnerabilities in Cargo, npm, PyPI, or GitHub Actions themselves — report those to the respective platform. ## Supported Versions Security fixes land on `main` and the latest published release of each affected crate. Given Callisto is pre-1.0, older minor versions are not backported — upgrade to the latest release.

# Resolver Version 3

Based on the documentation, here's what you need to know about resolver version 3:

## What Resolver "3" Does

Resolver version `"3"` changes the default behavior for handling Rust version compatibility:

**Changes the default for [`resolver.incompatible-rust-versions`](config.html#resolverincompatible-rust-versions) from `allow` to `fallback`**

This means the resolver will prefer packages with a Rust version that is less than or equal to your own Rust version, rather than allowing incompatible versions.

## Default per Edition

- `"3"` is the **default for `edition = "2024"`**

## Minimum Rust Version Required

**Requires Rust 1.84+**

## How to Enable

You can explicitly specify resolver version 3 in your `Cargo.toml`:

```toml
[package]
name = "my-package"
version = "1.0.0"
resolver = "3"
```

Or in a virtual workspace:

```toml
[workspace]
members = ["member1", "member2"]
resolver = "3"
```

## Key Behavior Change

With the `fallback` setting (default in v3), when resolving dependencies, the resolver prefers versions compatible with your package's minimum Rust version. For example, with Rust 1.85 and a package requiring Rust 1.62, version 4.0.32 (Rust 1.60.0) would be preferred over version 4.5.20 (Rust 1.74.0), even though 4.5.20 is newer.

# cargo publish Features

Based on the documentation, here's what `cargo publish` supports:

## Workspace and Multiple Package Support

**Yes**, `cargo publish` supports:

- **`--workspace`**: Publish all members in the workspace
- **`-p` / `--package`**: Publish only specified packages (supports glob patterns)
- **`--exclude`**: Exclude specified packages (works with `--workspace`)

Example:
```bash
cargo publish --workspace
cargo publish -p my_package
cargo publish --workspace --exclude my_package
```

**Yes**, `cargo publish` supports:

- **`--dry-run`**: Perform all checks without uploading
- **`--no-verify`**: Skip verification by building contents

cargo publish --dry-run

Based on the search results, here's what was found about Rust 1.90 and the `cargo publish --workspace` feature:

## Rust 1.90 Stabilizes Workspace Publishing

Cargo now supports `cargo publish --workspace`, automatically publishing all crates in a workspace in the right order following any dependencies between them. This has long been possible with external tooling or manual ordering of individual publishes, but this brings the functionality into Cargo itself.

### Key Features

Native integration allows Cargo's publish verification to run a build across the full set of to-be-published crates as if they were published, including during dry-runs. This works with dry-run mode to verify builds before actual publishing, with all crates being built as if they were already published to catch potential issues early.

### Important Limitation

Publishes are still not atomic -- network errors or server-side failures can still lead to a partially published workspace.

This feature was previously only available on nightly Rust but was stabilized in Rust 1.90, which was released on September 18, 2025.

Based on the search results, here's information about crates.io trusted publishing with GitHub Actions and the `rust-lang/crates-io-auth-action`:

## Overview

Crates.io trusted publishing lets a GitHub Actions workflow publish a crate without storing a long-lived crates.io API token in GitHub Actions secrets.

## How It Works

Short-lived access tokens are granted via the OpenID Connect (OIDC) protocol to authenticate and authorize actions with the crates.io APIs. The `rust-lang/crates-io-auth-action` exchanges this for a 30-minute access token.

## Configuration Requirements

Every workflow that publishes to crates.io through trusted publishing needs:
- a job with environment: <publish-environment>;
- permissions: id-token: write on that job, so GitHub can issue an OIDC token;

# crates-io-auth-action Overview

## Purpose
This GitHub Action retrieves temporary access tokens from crates.io for authenticated package publishing using trusted publishing.

## Usage Example
The action outputs a token that you can use in subsequent workflow steps:

```yaml
- name: Authenticate with custom registry
  id: auth
  uses: rust-lang/crates-io-auth-action@v1
  with:
    url: https://staging.crates.io
```

## Key Features

**Token Management:** The action automatically revokes the temporary token when your job completes, handling cleanup via its post-step.

**Custom Registry Support:** You can specify alternative registry URLs (like staging environments) instead of the default `https://crates.io`.

**Authentication Flow:** The tool requests a JWT token from GitHub, exchanges it with crates.io for a temporary token, and then revokes that token upon completion.

## Important Notes

- Review the [crates.io documentation](https://crates.io/docs/trusted-publishing) for comprehensive configuration details
- The project is dual-licensed under MIT and Apache 2.0
- Currently has 45 stars and 6 forks on GitHub

# Rust Version (MSRV) in Cargo

## Overview

The `rust-version` field specifies the **Minimum Supported Rust Version (MSRV)** for your package:

```toml
[package]
rust-version = "1.56"
```

**Format:** Must be a bare version number (e.g., `1.56`) with at least one component—no semver operators or pre-release identifiers.

## Key Uses

### Diagnostics
- Cargo reports an error when compiled on unsupported toolchains
- Provides clear support expectations instead of cryptic compilation errors
- Users can override with `--ignore-rust-version` flag

### Development Aid
- `cargo add` automatically selects dependency versions compatible with your `rust-version`
- The resolver considers Rust version when picking dependencies
- Tools like `cargo clippy` can lint against incompatible MSRVs

## Support Expectations

**Complete:** All functionality available on supported Rust versions under every feature

**Verified:** Functionality tested on supported Rust versions (automated CI testing)

**Patchable:** Users can override dependencies with forks that work on supported versions

**Dependency Support:** Each dependency version must support at least one version compatible with your `rust-version`

## Recommended Policies

Common approaches for selecting versions:

- **"N-2"** – Latest version with 2-release grace window
- **Even releases** – Every even release with 2-release grace window  
- **Calendar year** – All versions from current year with 1-year grace window

> **Tip:** Find your minimum compatible version with [`cargo-msrv`](https://crates.io/crates/cargo-msrv)

## Verifying MSRV in CI

Use tools to automate verification:

- **`cargo-msrv`** – Find and verify minimum supported version
- **`cargo-hack`** – Verify specific packages under specific Rust versions
- Standard `cargo` commands with `+<version>` toolchain specification

## Resolver Interplay

- When using multiple policies in a workspace, all shared dependencies must use the **lowest common compatible version**
- This may limit feature access for workspace members with higher `rust-version`
- With [`incompatible-rust-versions = "fallback"`](config.html#resolverincompatible-rust-versions), one package's Rust version can affect dependency selection for others

## Semver Implications

> Changing `rust-version` is a **minor incompatibility** per semver

Establish and document your policy clearly so users can align their own support schedules accordingly.

# cargo-semver-checks: Key Technical Details

## CI Integration
The project provides a GitHub Action for automated checking: "use as a [GitHub Action](https://github.com/obi1kenobi/cargo-semver-checks-action) (used in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` in this repo)" with configuration as simple as:
```yaml
- name: Check semver
  uses: obi1kenobi/cargo-semver-checks-action@v2
```

## Workspace Support
The tool supports workspace-level lint configuration through `[workspace.metadata.cargo-semver-checks.lints]`, allowing teams to define consistent semver policies across multiple crates.

## Baseline Requirements
Baselines can be sourced from multiple locations:
- **crates.io** (default for published crates)
- Git revisions via `--baseline-rev`
- Local directories with `--baseline-root`
- Pre-generated rustdoc JSON with `--baseline-rustdoc`

The tool accommodates unpublished crates through these alternative baseline methods.

## Lint Count & Coverage
The tool performs "dozens" of checks, though it explicitly acknowledges gaps: "it will not — not yet!" catch every violation. Common undetected issues include breaking type changes and generic/lifetime modifications.

## MSRV Policy
"MSRV bumps are _not_ considered major changes." The tool maintains separate compile-time and runtime MSRVs due to rustdoc JSON format instability, with runtime MSRV updates preferentially occurring in minor version bumps.

## Exit Codes
The tool uses distinct exit statuses: `0` for success, `100` for semver violations, and `101` for execution failures.

    description: 'Where to obtain Callisto: auto installs the requested release version; local builds validated Callisto checkout source and ignores version. Release jobs must use local.'
    required: false
    default: 'auto'
  version:

      own invocation is pinned to (github.action_ref resolved against callisto@ tags), falling
      back to the newest published release when that ref is unset or unresolvable.
    required: false
    default: 'latest'

    description: >-
      Attestation verification of the prebuilt release asset (gh attestation verify, repo
      orin-dx/callisto, signer workflow callisto-release.yml). One of: require = a failed
      verification or missing gh aborts the step and the asset is never run; fallback (default) =
      on failure or missing gh, warn, delete the asset and install from crates.io instead (never

Contributing to Callisto

By participating in this project, you agree to abide by the [Code of Conduct](./CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). Found a security issue? See [SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md) instead of opening a public issue. Agent-specific rules (invariants, fixing-bugs workflow, specs/plans, crate/license table) live in [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md) — this file covers human setup and PR process and does not duplicate them. How the code fits together: [ARCHITECTURE.md](./ARCHITECTURE.md) and [docs/architecture/](./docs/architecture/). --- ## Setup - Rust toolchain: pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml`, installed via `rustup`. - [`just`](https://github.com/casey/just): command runner for all workspace recipes. - [`moon`](https://moonrepo.dev): a few recipes (`build`, `fmt`, `fmt-check`, `lint-affected`) delegate to it; installed like any other tool via [proto](https://moonrepo.dev/proto) (`proto/callisto.toml` shows the same pattern for installing `callisto` itself). ```bash git clone https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto.git cd callisto just hooks # installs .git/hooks/pre-commit and pre-push just ci # full local verification pipeline ``` bug_report.md 585B feature_request.md 540B moon = "2"

## Callisto Rust 1.0 readiness audit (read-only; origin/main d1f0de357, v0.11.0)

All four libraries are already on crates.io at 0.11.0, so a semver baseline exists. No cargo build, test or clippy was run. `cargo machete` and `cargo package --list --offline` were the only tools executed. Unverified or from-memory items are tagged [mem].

### Established facts and sources

- **Current stable is Rust 1.99.1 (2026-10-15)**, preceded by 1.99.0 (2026-10-01), 1.98.x and 1.97.x. Source: [RELEASES.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rust-lang/rust/master/RELEASES.md). This machine has cargo/rustc 1.98.1.
- **Edition 2024** shipped in 1.85 ([blog](https://blog.rust-lang.org/2025/02/20/Rust-1.85.0/), [edition guide](https://doc.rust-lang.org/edition-guide/rust-2024/index.html)). It makes `resolver = "3"` the default and `cargo new` generates it. Resolver 3 flips `resolver.incompatible-rust-versions` from `allow` to `fallback`, so dependency selection prefers versions compatible with your `rust-version` ([resolver docs](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/resolver.html)). Let-chains are edition-2024-only; they stabilized around 1.88 [mem].
- **`cargo publish --workspace`** (also `-p` and `--exclude`) is stable since 1.90. It publishes in dependency order and verifies by building the whole set as if published, including under `--dry-run`. It is still not atomic ([1.90 blog](https://blog.rust-lang.org/2025/09/18/Rust-1.90.0/), [cargo-publish](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-publish.html)).
- **Trusted Publishing for crates.io** is GitHub-Actions-only. The first release must be published manually. The job needs `id-token: write`. `rust-lang/crates-io-auth-action@v1` exchanges the OIDC token for a short-lived token and revokes it in its post step ([blog](https://blog.rust-lang.org/2025/07/11/crates-io-development-update-2025-07), [action](https://github.com/rust-lang/crates-io-auth-action)). Search snippets also mention an `environment:` requirement and a 30-minute token ([forge docs](https://forge.rust-lang.org/infra/docs/trusted-publishing.html)). I could not fetch crates.io's own docs page, so confirm the environment rule there before relying on it.
- **MSRV guidance:** `rust-version` is advisory plus resolver input. Recommended policies are N-2, even releases, or calendar-based. MSRV should be verified in CI with `cargo-msrv`, `cargo-hack` or `cargo +<ver>`. Changing it is a "minor incompatibility" ([rust-version](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/rust-version.html)).
- **cargo-semver-checks** has a GitHub Action `obi1kenobi/cargo-semver-checks-action@v2`. It supports `--baseline-rev` and a workspace lint config, and it does not catch everything ([repo](https://github.com/obi1kenobi/cargo-semver-checks)).
- **Latest crates.io versions** (API, 2026-10-20): thiserror 2.0.21, toml 1.1.8, toml_edit 0.25.17, petgraph 0.8.3, schemars 1.2.3, rstest 0.28.0, dialoguer 0.12.0, comfy-table 8.0.1, similar 3.2.0, yaml-rust2 0.13.0, clap 4.6.7, miette 7.6.0, jsonschema 0.59.0 (e.g. [thiserror](https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/thiserror)).

### MSRV / edition / toolchain recommendation

| Setting | Now | Recommend |
| --- | --- | --- |
| edition | 2021 (`Cargo.toml:4`) | **2024** for workspace and `fuzz/Cargo.toml`. Run `cargo fix --edition` and expect `unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn` and tail-expression-temporary churn. The change is internal to binaries and not semver-visible. Do it before 1.0 so 1.0 is not edition-stale. |
| resolver | `"2"` explicit (`Cargo.toml:2`) | Drop the line or set `"3"`; 2024 implies it. |
| rust-version | 1.96 in `[workspace.package]` only | State an N-2 policy. At today's stable (1.99) that is **1.97**, or keep 1.96 only if CI proves it. Edition 2024 needs 1.85, so the floor is not constrained by the edition. |
| toolchain | `channel = "stable"` (`rust-toolchain.toml`) | Fine for dev. Add a separate MSRV CI job; today the floor is never tested. |

### Ranked gaps

**Must-fix before 1.0**

1. **Per-crate metadata is not inherited.**
   - Evidence: `crates/*/Cargo.toml` set only `edition.workspace` and `repository.workspace`. `rust-version`, `homepage`, `documentation`, `keywords` and `categories` exist only in `[workspace.package]` (`Cargo.toml:5-12`) and are never inherited.
   - Impact: published crates carry no `rust-version`, so Cargo's MSRV-aware resolution cannot help consumers, and the crates have no keywords, categories or docs link.
   - Fix: add `rust-version.workspace = true`, `keywords.workspace = true`, `categories.workspace = true` and `homepage.workspace = true` to every crate. Per-crate `documentation` should be docs.rs, not `docs.rs/callisto-cli` (workspace-level `documentation` is wrong for the libraries). Effort S.

2. **MSRV is declared but never verified.**
   - Evidence: `.github/workflows/callisto-ci.yml` has no MSRV job, and `rust-toolchain.toml` pins `stable`. The lockfile holds fresh majors (`syn` 3.0.3, `winnow` 1.0.4, `toml_edit` 0.25) whose MSRVs are unknown.
   - Impact: the 1.96 claim may be false, and users on that toolchain would find out at install time.
   - Fix: add a CI job `cargo +<msrv> check --workspace --locked`, and optionally `cargo hack check --rust-version` ([mem] for cargo-hack syntax). Also run `cargo install callisto-cli --locked` in a smoke test. Effort S.

3. **No semver gate, and the public API surface is enormous.**
   - Evidence: `just check-api` exists (`justfile`) but CI never calls it. All modules are `pub mod` in `crates/callisto-model/src/lib.rs`, `callisto-graph/src/lib.rs` and `callisto-cli/src/lib.rs`.
   - Counts of `pub` items: model 514, graph 357, cli 107, manifests 69. `callisto-cli` is a binary whose library target is fully public.
   - Impact: 1.0 on the libraries commits you to a SemVer promise over roughly 1000 pub items. That is likely not intended; the product is the CLI.

### Established facts and sources

- **Current stable is Rust 1.99.1 (2026-10-15)**, preceded by 1.99.0 (2026-10-01), 1.98.x and 1.97.x. Source: [RELEASES.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rust-lang/rust/master/RELEASES.md). This machine has cargo/rustc 1.98.1.
- **Edition 2024** shipped in 1.85 ([blog](https://blog.rust-lang.org/2025/02/20/Rust-1.85.0/), [edition guide](https://doc.rust-lang.org/edition-guide/rust-2024/index.html)). It makes `resolver = "3"` the default and `cargo new` generates it. Resolver 3 flips `resolver.incompatible-rust-versions` from `allow` to `fallback`, so dependency selection prefers versions compatible with your `rust-version` ([resolver docs](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/resolver.html)). Let-chains are edition-2024-only; they stabilized around 1.88 [mem].
- **`cargo publish --workspace`** (also `-p` and `--exclude`) is stable since 1.90. It publishes in dependency order and verifies by building the whole set as if published, including under `--dry-run`. It is still not atomic ([1.90 blog](https://blog.rust-lang.org/2025/09/18/Rust-1.90.0/), [cargo-publish](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-publish.html)).
- **Trusted Publishing for crates.io** is GitHub-Actions-only. The first release must be published manually. The job needs `id-token: write`. `rust-lang/crates-io-auth-action@v1` exchanges the OIDC token for a short-lived token and revokes it in its post step ([blog](https://blog.rust-lang.org/2025/07/11/crates-io-development-update-2025-07), [action](https://github.com/rust-lang/crates-io-auth-action)). Search snippets also mention an `environment:` requirement and a 30-minute token ([forge docs](https://forge.rust-lang.org/infra/docs/trusted-publishing.html)). I could not fetch crates.io's own docs page, so confirm the environment rule there before relying on it.
- **MSRV guidance:** `rust-version` is advisory plus resolver input. Recommended policies are N-2, even releases, or calendar-based. MSRV should be verified in CI with `cargo-msrv`, `cargo-hack` or `cargo +<ver>`. Changing it is a "minor incompatibility" ([rust-version](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/rust-version.html)).
- **cargo-semver-checks** has a GitHub Action `obi1kenobi/cargo-semver-checks-action@v2`. It supports `--baseline-rev` and a workspace lint config, and it does not catch everything ([repo](https://github.com/obi1kenobi/cargo-semver-checks)).
